title: Shared Brand Kit logo dialog exposes editing commands in a read-only view
impact: A recipient opening a shared logo sees Replace and Delete beside legitimate download options, despite the containing shared Kit having no editing controls. This makes the scope of the shared view harder to understand.
classification: Directly observed UI difference with source-confirmed read-only context
confidence: High for the visible commands and the current canEdit=false guest consumer. No stored-data write or security behaviour claimed.
roleEvidenceScope: Guest shared-link context rendered with underlying Studio Staff preview. isGuest forces canEdit=false independently of the three prototype roles; those three values were not separately repeated.
observed: The shared Kit hides page-level editing. Opening Loom horizontal - dark opens Download logo with a normal Replace button; its More actions menu contains Delete. Neither action was invoked. LogoDownloadModal has no canEdit parameter and unconditionally renders those actions.
expected: Nested dialogs should preserve the containing view capability. A read-only shared Kit should present logo preview and permitted downloads consistently with its page-level actions.
authority: Current shared route explicitly renders BrandKitPage with isGuest at src/app/share/brand/[token]/page.tsx17.
BrandKitContext.tsx136 defines canEdit as false whenever isGuest is true; this is the existing consumer contract, not a newly proposed permission model.
User audit requirement: judge task clarity and misleading controls, while keeping meaningful action distinctions.
recommendation: Pass the existing canEdit capability into LogoDownloadModal and omit Replace and the editing-only More actions menu in the shared view. Preserve its preview and download options and preserve these editing commands in editable Kits.
rationale: This is the smallest coherent presentation correction: the nested surface inherits the capability already used by its parent, without changing who may edit a normal Client Kit.
alternatives: A visible disabled editing state with a short reason could teach capability boundaries, but adds noise to a delivery-focused logo dialog. Hiding editing commands is clearer for the shared recipient.
tradeoffs: Do not remove Replace/Delete from legitimate editable Studio or Client Kits. Do not change guest persistence or invent new access rules as part of this visual correction.
rootCause: LogoDownloadModal renders an unconditional editing footer instead of consuming the parent capability.
occurrences: Shared Brand Kit > Logos > any selected logo uses the same LogoDownloadModal. Only the Loom horizontal - dark instance was directly opened.

evidence.approvedReferenceStatement: No approved screenshot of a shared logo-dialog variant exists. Current page-level read-only presentation and the explicit current canEdit contract provide the comparison; G012 is current UI evidence, not an approved visual reference.

approvedReference: No approved shared-logo dialog screenshot exists. G012 is the matching current read-only page, not an approved reference.
reproductionSteps: Open the valid current shared Brand Kit route /share/brand/loom-2026.
Observe page-level editing controls are absent.
Open Loom horizontal - dark in Logos.
Observe Replace; open More actions and observe Delete.
Close the menu/dialog without selecting Replace or Delete.
verificationRemaining: After any approved UI change, inspect valid shared and normal editable Kit consumers at1440 and1133.
Confirm shared logo preview/download affordances remain available and editable Studio/Client Kits retain their legitimate editing commands.
Actual Replace/Delete outcomes were deliberately not invoked; guest stored persistence is excluded and no write bypass is alleged.
